claims.claim: The loon analysis used more than 45,000 breeding records from 3,421 lakes, with declines of 0.5 to 2.5 percent a year, and northern Maine was relatively stable.
claims.episode_span: Declines ranged from 0.5 to 2.5 percent a year
claims.source_title: Scientists report ‘substantial’ declines in loons across Canada
claims.supporting_quote: The results mostly showed declines, ranging from 0.5 to 2.5 per cent per year, over a time period of two to four decades depending on available data. The exception was northern Maine, where loon productivity has been relatively stable.

claims.claim: Walter Piper said the study likely detects the leading edge of a broad loon decline and that northern data were unlikely to offset southern declines.

claims.source_title: Scientists report ‘substantial’ declines in loons across Canada
claims.supporting_quote: “We are probably detecting the leading edge of a broad decline in the loon population that is likely to continue in coming decades,” Dr. Piper said.
